goals.primary: Stay healthy to the start line

zones.threshold: 155-164 (not used this cycle - no dedicated threshold sessions; MP 8:30 sits well below this zone)

tibRules: Flare trigger is SUSTAINED fast pace in the 7:30-7:45 band, not volume or consecutive days. Nothing in this plan is scheduled faster than 8:00/mi, so that band is never approached.

The fastest sustained work in the block is the Wednesday tempo session, in weeks 4, 6, 8, 12 and 14 only, always at 8:00-8:15 and never faster. Rep length progresses deliberately: 3 x 0.5 mi (wk 4), 3 x 0.75 mi (wk 6), then 2 x 1 mi (wks 8, 12, 14). Broken reps with easy floats are used early to limit continuous time under tension while the stimulus is new; rep length extends only off clean morning-after checks. Shorter reps do not license faster paces. 8:00 is a firm floor at every rep length, and pace creep is the primary risk to monitor.
Marathon pace 8:30 is the race-specific workhorse and the only pace used in long-run pace-up segments. There is no dedicated threshold work this cycle.
Fast bursts (strides, <=90s reps) are safe but never sprint-fast. Strides run twice weekly throughout.
Long-run pace-up segments are capped at MP (8:30), built gradually within an easy base, and dropped immediately if the knee or tib speaks.
At most one dedicated tempo session per week, and at most one MP segment within that week's long run.
Morning-after check (touch-tenderness + stairs, for both knee and tib) governs progression, not in-run feel.

structure.Base: Weeks 1-5 (Jul 6 - Aug 9): 15.5 -> 23 mpw with a down week at wk5 (20.5). Easy aerobic + strides, knee return protocol wks 1-2, tempo enters wk4. LR 7.6 -> 11; first MP touch lands in the wk5 long run.
structure.Build: Weeks 6-11 (Aug 10 - Sep 20): 27 -> 35.5 mpw, dipping to 22.5 in the wk9 travel cutback. Easy aerobic + strides, tempo in wks 6 and 8, MP (8:30) segments grow inside the long run. LR 12.5 -> 17. No threshold work.
structure.Peak: Weeks 12-14 (Sep 21 - Oct 11): 40 -> 45 mpw with a long-run unload at wk13 (35 mpw, LR 15). LR 20 / 15 / 22, the 22 on Oct 10. Tempo in wks 12 and 14; wk14's is droppable if peak-week fatigue warrants.
structure.Taper: Weeks 15-17 (Oct 12 - Nov 1): volume drops to 30/24, then race week (~38 incl. race), short MP (8:30) touches to stay sharp, race Nov 1

days.focus: Full rest. Structural, not conditional. Morning tib check: touch-tenderness + first flight of stairs.

Third easy day in a row (5/6.5/4). Keep it genuinely easy - this is the biggest consecutive-day block you'll have done, but all easy pace so it's leg fatigue, not tib risk. Morning-after check tomorrow matters.

RACE DAY. Goal 3:43 at 8:30/mi, HR 148-153. Start controlled - bank nothing, let the first 10K feel almost easy. Settle into 8:30, fuel every 30-40 min. The knee and tib have been managed all block; race pace is safely outside your flare zone, so run your race. Adjust to what the day gives: sub-3:50 B-goal, and you beat 3:59 comfortably. Trust the block.
